FILE: /workspace/src/scene/transform.cpp
Implement `Mat4 Transform::local_to_world() const` and `Mat4 Transform::world_to_local() const` by composing TRS transforms up the scene-graph parent chain. Read /workspace/src/scene/transform.h first for the class layout (it has a `std::weak_ptr<Transform> parent`, `translation`, `rotation`, `scale`, and helpers `local_to_parent()` / `parent_to_local()` already implemented). Requirements: local_to_world composes local_to_parent() up the chain to the root; world_to_local is the reverse composition built from parent_to_local() — you MUST NOT call Mat4::inverse() anywhere. Handle a null/expired parent (root) correctly. Study /workspace/tests/a1/test.a1.task1.cpp to confirm exact expected semantics.

FILE: /workspace/src/geometry/halfedge-global.cpp
Implement these four stubs (leave triangulate/linear_subdivide/catmark_subdivide/loop_subdivide/isotropic_remesh/simplify stubs untouched):
1. `catmark_subdivide_helper(vertex_positions, edge_vertex_positions, face_vertex_positions)` — the topological Catmull-Clark split: for every edge, split it (same concept as split_edge applied to all edges — but note split_edge only splits non-boundary-adjacent faces appropriately; the classic approach is to bisect every edge then connect edge-center vertices to face-center vertices); then for every non-boundary face insert a face-center vertex and split the face into quads; finally assign positions: original vertices from vertex_positions, edge-split vertices from edge_vertex_positions, face-center vertices from face_vertex_positions. IMPORTANT: collect the original edges/faces BEFORE modifying (iterating while mutating invalidates loops); use split_edge on each original edge (it returns the new vertex), then for each original non-boundary face add the center vertex and connect. Use interpolate_data where new elements need corner/bone data (split_edge/bisect_edge already do this internally). Study /workspace/tests/a2/test.a2.g2.cpp and test.a2.g3.cpp — they exercise this helper via linear_subdivide/catmark_subdivide, but NOTE: those caller functions' position computations are other stubs you must NOT implement; the harness probes catmark_subdivide_helper directly, so make it correct as a standalone topological routine.
2. `flip_orientation()` — reverse winding of every face loop: no elements created/erased; only Halfedge::next, Halfedge::vertex, and Vertex::halfedge pointers change (per the header comment). The standard trick: each halfedge keeps its edge but swaps roles with its twin — swap next pointers appropriately and set each halfedge's vertex to its twin's old vertex (i.e. reverse each face cycle).
3. `set_corner_normals(float threshold)` — per-corner shading normals with smoothing groups: threshold >= 180 => all edges smooth; threshold <= 0 => all edges sharp; otherwise an edge is sharp if its sharp flag is set OR the dihedral angle between adjacent face normals (in degrees) exceeds threshold. For each corner (halfedge), the corner normal is the area-weighted average of the normals of the faces reachable by fanning around the vertex without crossing a sharp edge (the smoothing group containing that halfedge's face). Boundary faces are excluded from normal accumulation. Normalize results. Read halfedge-utility.cpp for Face::normal()/Vertex::normal() helpers. Check /workspace/tests for any a2 tests touching normals.
4. `set_corner_uvs_per_face()` — assign corner UVs by projecting each face's vertices onto a tangent plane perpendicular to the face normal: build an orthonormal basis (u,v) from the face normal and set each corner_uv = (dot(pos,u), dot(pos,v)) (boundary faces get (0,0), matching set_corner_uvs_project's convention which you can read in the same file).
Study tests in /workspace/tests/a2/test.a2.global.mix.cpp for how helper/subdivision results are diffed.

FILE: /workspace/src/geometry/halfedge-local.cpp
Implement these six stubs (leave the other optional stubs like bevel_vertex/inset_vertex/dissolve_* untouched):
1. `bisect_edge(EdgeRef e)` — split edge at midpoint without dividing adjacent faces. Allocate 1 vertex, 2 halfedges, 1 edge; rewire all twin/next/vertex/edge/face pointers; works when either side is a boundary face; call interpolate_data({v1,v2}, new_vertex) and interpolate_data for the new halfedges' corner data per the usage examples in halfedge.h. Study /workspace/tests/a2/test.a2.l2.cpp (bisect cases) and test.a2.local.mix.cpp.
2. `split_edge(EdgeRef e)` — call bisect_edge first, then split each adjacent NON-boundary face by connecting the new midpoint vertex to the vertex ccw from the ccw-most end of e within the face (works for general polygons, not just triangles). The new vertex's halfedge must lie along the original edge e. Study test.a2.l2.cpp carefully for the exact expected topology (which new halfedge/edge/face gets which id matters because tests diff against from_indexed_faces-built meshes).
3. `flip_edge(EdgeRef e)` — rotate a non-boundary edge CCW within its two containing faces, generalized to arbitrary polygon faces (draw the general-polygon case: the edge moves one vertex over on each side). No allocation/erasure. Return std::nullopt for boundary edges or if the result would be non-manifold/invalid (e.g. would create a face with <3 sides or a duplicate edge — validate via a manifoldness check). Study test.a2.l1.cpp.
4. `collapse_edge(EdgeRef e)` — merge endpoints into one vertex at the midpoint, removing the edge; adjacent triangle faces degenerate and must be removed properly (their other edges get merged), general polygon faces just lose the edge. Detect and reject (return std::nullopt, mesh unchanged) collapses that would produce a non-manifold mesh (the standard check: the intersection of the two endpoints' one-rings must be exactly the vertices opposite the edge in adjacent faces). Use interpolate_data({v1,v2}, merged_vertex) and for merged halfedge corner data. Study test.a2.l3.cpp.
5. `extrude_face(FaceRef f)` — create an inset copy of the face surrounded by new quad side faces; new vertices start at the SAME positions as the originals (see the [BEVEL NOTE] comment in the file). Return the new inner face. Use interpolate_data for new vertices/halfedges. Study test.a2.l4.cpp.
6. `extrude_positions(FaceRef face, Vec3 move, float shrink)` — position update applied to a face created by extrude_face: move each vertex of the inner face toward the face's original centroid by `shrink` (0 = no shrink, 1 = point) then translate by `move`. Only positions change.
All operations must preserve halfedge invariants (mesh passes validate()) and handle boundary-adjacent cases correctly.
